sections.history: Thirumohur is a village in the paddy country a short drive north-east of Madurai, and its temple is one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Pandya Nadu. Its lord is Kalamegha Perumal — the name likens him to the dark rain-cloud that brings life to parched fields — and the Goddess is Mohanavalli Thayar. The place is also called Mohanapuram, the town of Mohini, after the legend at its heart. Nammalvar sang the lord of Thirumohur in his Tiruvaimozhi, as the refuge who answers those who call to him in danger, and Thirumangai Alvar is also remembered among those who praised the shrine. The temple has long been one of the cluster of Vishnu shrines around Madurai visited together by pilgrims.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner of the Pandya country, entered through a gateway tower and gathered around the sanctum of Kalamegha Perumal, with Mohanavalli Thayar in a separate shrine. Its most famous image is in the shrine of Chakrathalvar, the personified discus Sudarshana: he bears sixteen weapons in sixteen arms, and on the back of the same stone is carved Narasimha, so that the two are worshipped as one.
sections.legends: The sthala purana places here the episode from the churning of the ocean when Vishnu took the bewitching form of Mohini, drawing the asuras away so that the devas received the nectar of immortality — hence the names Mohanapuram and Mohanavalli. Another account tells that a drop of the nectar fell into the temple tank, and the lord appeared on its southern bank. Tradition also holds that Brahma worshipped Vishnu here after the Vedas were rescued from the demons Madhu and Kaitabha.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava festivals of the year, among them Vaikunta Ekadashi, with processions of the utsava deities through the village streets. Devotees come in particular to worship at the Chakrathalvar shrine, offering prayers for protection and the removal of obstacles.
sections.experience: A quieter Divya Desam than the great Madurai temples, easily added to a day among the Vishnu shrines around the city. Linger at the Chakrathalvar shrine and walk round to see Narasimha on its reverse — a rare double image. Morning visits are calm, and the village setting among fields keeps the atmosphere unhurried.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirumohur lies near Othakadai, roughly 10–12 km north-east of Madurai by road, with local buses and taxis from the city. Madurai Junction is the nearest major railway station and Madurai Airport the nearest airport.
